riskReasons: Accepted name, taxon, dissected leaf form and red-purple seasonal sequence are consistently supported.
Published dimensions differ by framework and age but do not imply different identities.
No material synonym or commercial-alias conflict was found.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with all RC-001–RC-010 records and all other approved Catalogue assignments. It is distinct from RC-004 ‘Crimson Queen’ and from CUL-000020 ‘Red Dragon’, CUL-000021 ‘Tamukeyama’ and CUL-000022 ‘Orangeola’: the reviewed sources describe a relatively vigorous upright-rounded yet cascading plant with its own name history and size profile. C0 resolves as unique.

identityNotes: The accepted working name follows the RHS hyphenated accepted form. The designation ‘var. dissectum’ used in some horticultural sources is a group-style placement, not a separate cultivar identity. The misspelling ‘Inaba Shidara’ is not accepted as a governed variant.

content.summary: A vigorous red-purple laceleaf Japanese maple combining arching, cascading branches with deeply dissected foliage that remains purple-red through much of the growing season and becomes bright crimson-red in autumn.
content.habit: Small deciduous shrub or tree with arching branches and a rounded, cascading outline. It may be trained higher but usually spreads at least as widely as it grows tall.
content.leafForm: Large, deeply divided laceleaf foliage, commonly described with seven strongly incised lobes. The foliage is finer than ordinary palmate leaves but can appear broader and more substantial than some compact red dissectum cultivars.

seasonal.spring: Leaves emerge deep purple; small reddish flowers may be visible at close range.
seasonal.summer: Foliage matures to purple-red and may vary in depth with exposure and heat.
seasonal.autumn: Leaves turn crimson to bright red.

size.qualifier: RHS gives 1.5–2.5 m high and wide; Missouri Botanical Garden gives 6–10 ft high and 8–15 ft wide. Ranges are source- and age-dependent.

content.cultivation: Grow in moist, organically rich, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, with afternoon protection in hotter regions. Avoid hot, dry and wind-exposed sites, and maintain moisture to reduce scorch.
content.diagnostic: Compared with RC-004 ‘Crimson Queen’, ‘Inaba-shidare’ is generally presented as more vigorous and more upright before cascading, with relatively large deep-purple dissected leaves. These tendencies aid comparison but do not authenticate an individual plant without provenance.
content.confidence: High confidence in identity, dissected leaf form, arching-cascading habit and broad colour sequence; moderate confidence in mature size because institutional ranges differ substantially.
content.unresolvedIssue: Published mature dimensions differ, and this lean review does not establish a universal size ceiling or authenticate unlabeled plants circulating in commerce.
